title: Credibility assessment of CFD models for intravascular catheter trackability and flow resistance using ASME V&V40
device: Hydrophilic-coated 5F intravascular diagnostic catheter with distal side-holes

models.name: ResistiveFlow-CFD
models.what_it_computes: Steady, incompressible CFD of internal catheter flow and annular vessel flow to quantify pressure drop, minor-loss coefficients, and wall shear related to flow resistance.

models.name: AdvancementCFD
models.what_it_computes: Unsteady CFD with prescribed catheter-tip kinematics in a curved vessel to estimate hydrodynamic force and moment vectors that affect trackability during advancement.

mechanisms.name: M1: Shaft friction and distributed losses
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Determines baseline pressure drop across the catheter for contrast/infusate delivery and hemodynamic impact during routine use.

mechanisms.name: M2: Tip and side-hole entrance/exit losses
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Adds localized resistance that can dominate total flow penalty at clinically relevant rates and influences jet-induced flow patterns.

mechanisms.name: M3: Hydrodynamic steering and damping in curvature
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Fluid forces at the advancing tip alter effective pushability and path stability, affecting trackability through tortuous segments.

mechanisms.name: M4: Flow-mediated wall contact pressure at the tip
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Pressure asymmetries around the tip modulate sticking/unsticking behavior during advancement, influencing trackability and procedure time.

clear_factors: Relevance of the quantities of interest
Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

deviation.detail: All credibility factors are scored on a 0–5 integer scale (0=no evidence, 5=compelling evidence) per model–mechanism pair and used to judge adequacy.

sections: Background and objective: to establish credibility of CFD predictions for catheter flow resistance and trackability in support of premarket design selection and bench test prioritization
Device and clinical decision context: 5F hydrophilic diagnostic catheter with distal side-holes; performance endpoints are pressure drop over flow rate and trackability through tortuous paths

Context of Use (CoU) and Model Risk: CoU—use model outputs to inform design selection and specify bench test configurations/acceptance thresholds for pressure drop and advancement stability; not for patient-specific clinical decisions. Model risk—medium, because erroneous predictions could lead to suboptimal design choices and longer procedures, but decisions are mitigated by bench testing and clinical reviews (rationale: outputs influence design and test setup but are not the sole basis for clinical decision-making).
Computational models: overview of ResistiveFlow-CFD (steady, laminar regimes, minor-loss estimation) and AdvancementCFD (transient, prescribed tip motion, hydrodynamic force/moment extraction)
Mechanisms addressed: mapping M1–M4 to resistance and trackability endpoints; linkage between QoIs and acceptance criteria

Credibility factors and scoring method: factors limited to Model inputs; Numerical solver error; Output comparison; Relevance of the quantities of interest; Relevance of the validation activities to the COU; Test conditions; Use error. Credibility levels reported on the 0–5 scale for each model–mechanism pair.

ResistiveFlow-CFD × M1 (Shaft friction and distributed losses)—Credibility scoring (0–5): Model inputs=4; Numerical solver error=4; Output comparison=5; Relevance of the quantities of interest=5; Relevance of the validation activities to the COU=4; Test conditions=3; Use error=2.

ResistiveFlow-CFD × M2 (Tip and side-hole entrance/exit losses)—Credibility scoring (0–5): Model inputs=4; Numerical solver error=3; Output comparison=4; Relevance of the quantities of interest=4; Relevance of the validation activities to the COU=4; Test conditions=3; Use error=2.

AdvancementCFD × M3 (Hydrodynamic steering and damping in curvature)—Credibility scoring (0–5): Model inputs=3; Numerical solver error=3; Output comparison=3; Relevance of the quantities of interest=5; Relevance of the validation activities to the COU=3; Test conditions=2; Use error=2.

AdvancementCFD × M4 (Flow-mediated wall contact pressure at the tip)—Credibility scoring (0–5): Model inputs=3; Numerical solver error=2; Output comparison=3; Relevance of the quantities of interest=4; Relevance of the validation activities to the COU=3; Test conditions=2; Use error=2.

Model inputs: parameterization sources, measurement methods, and sensitivity highlights supporting the assigned scores (e.g., lumen ID/OD, fluid viscosity range, curvature metrics, prescribed tip kinematics)
Numerical solver error: mesh/temporal refinement strategies and residual criteria supporting the assigned scores for steady and unsteady cases
Output comparison: bench flow-loop datasets for pressure drop and phantom advancement datasets for hydrodynamic force proxies; error metrics and acceptance thresholds
Relevance of the quantities of interest: alignment of ΔP, loss coefficients, and tip force/moment vectors with performance endpoints and design decisions
Relevance of the validation activities to the COU: mapping of validation scenarios to intended use decisions (design selection and test setup specification)
Test conditions: physiological ranges and boundary conditions approximated in simulations and tests (not exhaustive but consistent with intended operating envelope)
Use error: handling of operator-dependent inputs (e.g., prescribed advancement path and insertion speed) and implications for reproducibility during deployment
Synthesis of credibility across mechanisms: adequacy judgments for resistance-related endpoints (high confidence) and trackability-related endpoints (moderate confidence) based on factor scores
Decision framework: acceptance of models for informing design and bench test specifications under the stated CoU; identification of factors requiring targeted improvement before expanding use

Conclusions: both models achieve acceptable credibility for the stated CoU at medium model risk; priorities include strengthening transient solver error control and broadening test conditions for trackability-related mechanisms
